claims.text: Larousse describes a royal appointment at Paris with an unresolved 1260 or 1261 date. Lyon’s archives distinguish royal sovereignty, archiepiscopal lordship and chartered bourgeois rights, with craftmasters electing consuls. These are different powers and constituencies. The lost charter is known through later copies; neither a crown label nor elected consuls establishes universal representation or unlimited taxation.
